:\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/i\u003E\u003C\/u\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EAdd 20 microliter of drawn blood specimen with a 20 microliter capillary pipette into the sample well. \u0026nbsp;OR\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EAdd 10 microliter of serum into the sample well —-\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EAdd 4 drops of assay diluent into sample mins\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cu\u003ENEGATIVE \u003C\/u\u003E: the presence of only control line (C) within the result window indicates negative result\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cu\u003EPOSITIVE\u003C\/u\u003E: * the presence of 2 lines as control line (c) and test line (l) with in the result window indicates result for HIV - 1\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E* The presence of 2 lines as control line (C) and test line (2) with in the result window indicates result for HIV - 2\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E* the presence of 3 lines as control line (C) , test line (1) and test line (2) with in the result window indicates a positive result for HIV - 1 \u0026amp; HIV - of serum with droppers to S well of the antibody device ( IgM,IgG ) and 2 drops of ( 70 microliter ) of buffer to the B well of the antibody device (IgM, IgG)\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Ci\u003E\u003Cu\u003EInterpretation:\u003C\/u\u003E\u003C\/i\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ERead the reaction at 20 mins . Positive results may appear as early as 2-10 mins. However negative results must be confirmed at 20 mins only\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cu\u003EInterpretation of NS1 Ag :\u003C\/u\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cb\u003EREACTIVE \u003C\/b\u003E: Appearance of pink coloured line , one in test region T and control region C that sample is non reactive for NS1 Ag\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cb\u003ENON REACTIVE\u003C\/b\u003E : Appearance of one distinct pink line on control region C only indicates that sample is non reactive for NS1 Ag\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cb\u003EInvalid\u003C\/b\u003E : neither control line nor the test line appears on membrane the \u0026nbsp;it is invalid\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cu\u003EInterpretation of IgM \u0026amp; IgG : \u0026nbsp;\u003C\/u\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cb\u003EIgM \u0026amp; IgG reactive\u003C\/b\u003E : Appearance of \u0026nbsp;red coloured line in the control region C and test region , IgM region M \u0026amp; IgG region G indicates that the sample os reactive for both IgM \u0026amp; IgG\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cb\u003EIgM reactive\u003C\/b\u003E : Appearance of red coloured line in the control region C and test region , \u0026nbsp;IgM region M indicates that the sample is reactive for IgM antibodies\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cb\u003EIgG reactive\u003C\/b\u003E : Appearance of red coloured line in the control region C and test region , IgG region G indicates that the sample is reactive for IgG antibodies\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cb\u003ENon reactive\u003C\/b\u003E : Appearance of one distinct red coloured line in the control region C with no line in the IgM \u0026amp; Discard 1 ml of diluted sample from tube no.6 of each set — tube no.7 in each set serves as antigen control — to all tubes of the respective sets add one drop of the respective antigen suspension and mix well. Cover and incubate at 37 degree Celsius for 16-20 hrs — look for agglutination\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EThe tubes 1-7 will give 1:20, 1:40, 1:80, 1:160, 1:320 and 1:640 dilutions\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EAdd 1 drop of respective antigens to all the tubes in each #d9ead3; caret-color: rgb(0, 0, 0);\"\u003E\u003Cdiv style=\"caret-color: rgb(86, 86, 86); font-size: 15.84px;\"\u003E\u003Cdiv style=\"font-size: 15.84px; font-weight: 400;\"\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv style=\"font-size: 15.84px; font-weight: 400;\"\u003E\u003Ci\u003E\u003Ca href=\"https:\/\/63konakanchihyndavi.blogspot.com\/2022\/12\/this-is-online-e-log-book-to-discuss.html\"\u003Ehttps:\/\/63konakanchihyndavi.blogspot.com\/2022\/12\/this-is-online-e-log-book-to-discuss.html\u003C\/a\u003E\u003C\/i\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv style=\"font-size: 15.84px; font-weight: 400;\"\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv style=\"font-size: 15.84px; font-weight: 400;\"\u003E\u003Ci\u003EI have assisted Dr.Chandana mam ( pgy3 ) in central line\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/i\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv style=\"font-size: 15.84px; font-weight: 400;\"\u003E\u003Ci\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/i\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv style=\"font-size: 15.84px;\"\u003E\u003Ci\u003E\u003Cb\u003EComing to ICU DUTIES \u003C\/b\u003E; I’ve had my ups and downs, even then they are most memorable internship duties till date.\u003C\/i\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv style=\"font-size: 15.84px; font-weight: 400;\"\u003E\u003Ci\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/i\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv style=\"font-size: 15.84px; font-weight: 400;\"\u003E\u003Ci\u003EBecause ; before ICU I didn’t do any procedure except for the 3 stictches in the surgical OT \u0026amp; regular ulcer dressings, this place gave me so much opportunity to learn ABG, RYLES TUBE, FOLEYS CATHETER , taking SAMPLES. I’ve taken approximately 25 ABG Till date and no doubt its because of icu duties ive learnt the technique.\u003C\/i\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv style=\"font-size: 15.84px; font-weight: 400;\"\u003E\u003Ci\u003EDid ascitic tap for a patient in Z TARCK \u0026nbsp;TECHNIQUE under the guidance of Dr.Haripriya mam ( pgy2 )\u003C\/i\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv style=\"font-size: 15.84px; font-weight: 400;\"\u003E\u003Ci\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/i\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv style=\"font-size: 15.84px; font-weight: 400;\"\u003E\u003Ci\u003E\u003Cu\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"color: #a64d79;\"\u003EMY EXPERIENCE OF ONE HECTIC ICU NIGHT DUTY:\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/u\u003E\u003C\/i\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv style=\"font-size: 15.84px; font-weight: 400;\"\u003E\u003Ci\u003EOn the second ICU bed there is an intubated patient with zero percent survival chance ; she had no peripheral pulses and her bp was not recordable from 10 pm. I’ve checked her carotid pulse every 15-20 mins :\/ may be just to give their attenders correct death time , at around 6 in the morning even carotid pulse was lost and then we started CPR ; for about 30 mins ; she regained the carotid pulse which was slow, irregular and prominent ( it mostly may be because of the drugs we gave her )\u0026amp; ECG was done and it didn’t show flat line ; it showed some strange pattern —after15 mins her pulse became fast, regular but less prominent — after 15 mins again her carotid pulse was lost — CPR was done again for 30 mins , but couldn’t revive the patient this time — ECG was done and it showed a flat line — patient was declared dead at around 7:40 am\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/i\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv style=\"font-size: 15.84px; font-weight: 400;\"\u003E\u003Ci\u003EOn the third bed there is ‘imaginary pillow case; who got intubated and extubated’ \u0026nbsp;on that day itself he was shifted to ICU from AMC for his SOB ; he wasn’t keeping on the oxygen mask and not listening to my words( his sats are dropping to 80 without oxygen mask) ;his wife is least bothered about all this \u0026amp; slept\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/i\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv style=\"font-size: 15.84px; font-weight: 400;\"\u003E\u003Ci\u003EOn the fourth bed there is case of Diabetic Ketoacidosis; for which I’ve given a chart to adjust the insulin infusion rate accordingly to hrly grbs ; the grbs values are persistently high during consecutive hrs in the night; but the point I didn’t observe is the NS fluid correction is not going well for the other hand as there is a block ; after noticing that I gave flush 1-2 times and by the late morning his sugar values came down\u003C\/i\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv style=\"font-size: 15.84px; font-weight: 400;\"\u003E\u003Ci\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/i\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv style=\"font-size: 15.84px; font-weight: 400;\"\u003E\u003Ci\u003ECOMING TO THE STRANGE PART; WHEN I’VE ENTERED ICU CPR AND INTUBATION WAS DONE FOR ONE CASE AND BY THE TIME I’VE LEFT \u0026nbsp;ICU THERE IS A DEATH OF ANOTHER INTUBATED CASE ; for my 1st icu duty when I entered at 8am ;there was a case in AMC - for which bp was not recordable — immediately the case is shifted to ICU and CPR was done; for this patient there was a central line procedure done by Dr. Narsimha sir ( pgy2 ) for which I’ve did the simple 2-2-1 suturing ;however, this patient died after 2 and 1\/2 days ; the other 2 1\/2 days of my 5 days icu posting is shared by the patient which was described above ( icu bed 2 ) and by the time I’ve completed my 5 days icu journey; she died\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/i\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv style=\"font-size: 15.84px; font-weight: 400;\"\u003E\u003Ci\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/i\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv style=\"font-size: 15.84px; font-weight: 400;\"\u003E\u003Ci\u003E\u0026nbsp;During my duties; in the free time Dr. DK sir(pgy3) explained me ECG \u0026amp; other concepts \u0026amp; Dr. Raveen sir ( pgy3) , Dr. Sai Charan sir ( pgy3 ) have explained some interesting concepts around the current admitted patients\u003C\/i\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv style=\"font-size: 15.84px; font-weight: 400;\"\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv style=\"font-size: 15.84px;\"\u003E\u003Ci\u003E\u003Cb\u003EI think in the ICU we need to become cold hearted , dumb, bold to do the duties ; every minute in there is challenging, it’s tougher than you think; you will become braver, stronger and smarter if you utilise your time wisely in ICU\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/i\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv style=\"font-size: 15.84px; font-weight: 400;\"\u003E\u003Ci\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/i\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv style=\"font-size: 15.84px; font-weight: 400;\"\u003E\u003Ci style=\"font-size: 15.84px;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"color: #a64d79;\"\u003EHOW ARE PT, INR TESTS DONE IN OUR LAB :\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/i\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv style=\"font-size: 15.84px; font-weight: 400;\"\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv style=\"font-size: 15.84px; font-weight: 400;\"\u003EFirst blood of the patient is collected in blue coloured vacutainer ( containing an anticoagulant- 3.2% sodium citrate) and then blood is centrifuged for 15 mins thereby separating the plasma from the cells\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv style=\"font-size: 15.84px; in response to this there is compensatory mechanism of beta cells of pancreas ; they start producing more and more insulin and at one point of time beta cells fail to produce insulin leading diabetes\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EDiabetes \u0026nbsp;can cause LVH\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EMechanism : diabetes causes AGEs (advanced glycation end products) accumulation causing ECM (Extra Cellular Matrix ) remodelling , myocyte apoptosis—fibrosis—LV CONCENTRIC HYPERTROPHY\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ESO IT IS EVIDENT THAT ; margin-right: 1em;\"\u003E\u003Cimg border=\"0\" data-original-height=\"654\" data-original-width=\"1128\" height=\"186\" src=\"https:\/\/blogger.googleusercontent.com\/img\/b\/R29vZ2xl\/AVvXsEiXi5FDhC3kyHQEB9lv_iO0h10FezO4FGBVNiEdKfyOrrXrxVQmsQJ1MvQMdGF96tsH20fU_-G0QmYD23L-ROg0Q3RasTxQzZfIpGhQd9g18xM414Jh9Z4GxdJFAaTGghXHBv47xT0NB0YtgzT3wlZkEPa2NYvniuyMhVr25n0x1sa6LGZB7-D7lGB1Yg\/s320\/31CD6AA4-58E3-46D5-B6CB-F65A1B0DFF79.jpeg\" width=\"320\" \/\u003E\u003C\/a\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cb\u003ESPEAKER NOTES FOR SLIDE NO.14\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EDISCUSSION ON PATHOPHYSIOLOGY OF CARDIOGENIC AND NON CARDIOGENIC PULMONARY EDEMA\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EIn case of cardiogenic pulmonary edema there is increased pressures in left side of heart and pressure is transmitted to LUNG THROUGH PULMONARY VEINS \u0026nbsp;, in the lung there is increased pulmonary capillary wedge pressure ; this leads to increased hydrostatic pressure in the blood capillaries at the alveolar end, there is fluid leak into alveoli and hence there is pulmonary edema but there is intact alveolar epithelial basement membrane \u0026amp; endothelial basement membrane, the fluid collected in the alveoli is purely of trasudative in nature\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EOn the other hand in case of non cardiogenic pulmonary edema for example in cases of pneumonia and ARDS , there is disruption of alveolar epithelial basement membrane \u0026amp; endothelial basement membrane initiated by pro inflammatory mediators IL 1, IL 8 \u0026amp; TNF ALPHA an later further inflammation is mediated by neutrophils which releases proteases and reactive oxygen species this cascade leads to fluid leak in to the alveoli but this time with neutrophil cells,inflammatory mediators, proteins \u0026amp; there are marked infalmmatory changes in the alveoli the fluid collected in the alveoli is of exudative in nature\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cb\u003ESLIDE NO.15\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\" style=\"clear: both;
